- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast increase to 3% max from prior day.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.67) but price declines sharply, model underreacts; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to match sentiment shift.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — if true price drops below 3σ from recent mean, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent trends; apply smoothing filter to avoid 2–3 consecutive day forecast increases.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment turns bearish after a peak, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–4% per day for 3–5 days following sentiment drop.
